357510.file-name: XC357510 - Collared Forest Falcon - Micrastur semitorquatus.mp3
357510.rmk:
The forest-falcon called from what sounded to be about 300 m away. I played its call (XC271370, then XC15730). About 30 seconds after playing the second call, he/she approached and landed on a branch about 80 m away and about 15 m high in a tree, in full view; it definitely was an adult. After about 45 seconds, he/she flew past us (within about 40 m) and disappeared out of view. About 5 minutes later, he/she started calling again, and I started recording. He/she was perched about 18 m high in a tree. This recording included 44 calls; he/she voiced about 8 before I started recording, so the entire bout was about 52 calls.
Examples of the background birds are: Tropical Gnatcatcher at 0:00, 0:23, 0:41; Lesser Greenlet at 0:16, 0:40, 0:52; Green Shrike-Vireo at 0:19; Scarlet-rumped Cacique at 0:30, 0:43; Fasciated Antshrike at 1:01, 3:03; Russet-winged Schiffornis at 1:26 (the only one); Short-billed Pigeon (very faint at 2:03); Yellow-margined Flatbill at 1:58; Yellow-crowned Tyrannulet at 1:39; and Paltry Tyrannulet at 2:42.
Howler monkeys can be heard throughout (e.g., 1:02).

The Collared Forest-Falcon was clearly visible as it was calling, although it was still too dark for a photograph.  This is a clip from a 3-minute recording, the WAV file of which is available upon request (along with additional WAV files of the same recording session).

**Description:** First call (0m02s) from individual perched in mango tree roughly 10m off ground. After a few seconds it starts to move upwards through the branches. At about 0m31s it encounters one or two other individuals that were hidden at the canopy, as they utter a distinct sort of vocalization. There may be a nest at the top of that tree, since at least one individual was seen flying off and back to that tree several times in a couple of days. Earlier the day of the recording, three individuals were seen flying together in circles in the neighbourhood.

**Habitat:** Urban backyard.

**Equipment:** Sony ICD-PX312 personal recorder.

This audio is in the background of a video of a White-throated Toucan, in Ecuadorian lowland amazon secondary rainforest.  Correctly identified by Niels Krabbe in the thread discussion. Thankyou Niels!

933181.rmk:
Áudio extraído de vídeo obtido com telefone celular Samsung A54 - https://youtu.be/cUYurwEoKpU?si=5dZ1FRuAQubq7BNt

Há 12 anos observo duas corujinhas-do-mato frequentando o quintal. Nesse período, percebi que elas apreciam um banho noturno. Ontem, logo ao anoitecer, eu estava repondo água na "piscininha" delas e percebi  que uma chegou - a primeira mostrada no vídeo. Comecei a filmar com o celular e ouvindo os "miadinhos" atrás de mim - logo virei na direção do som e vi a outra corujinha.

Não havia outras aves, nem sequer as corujas buraqueiras que às vezes também vem ao quintal.

406518.rmk:
Ave gravada em mata Atlântica de encosta, de fisionomia preservada, ao longo de um córrego florestal no bairro Sesmarias , em Ubatuba/SP, Brasil .
O Falcão passou a Vocalizar após um Spizaetus tyrannus passar voando e vocalizando acima do dossel da mata . Após alguns minutos com ele em silêncio, usei o playback da espécie para conseguir um registro , e eis que o Falcão iniciou essa longa vocalização que foi gravada até o fim do canto , perdendo apenas as primeiras notas (cerca de 5 segundos) , pois foi o tempo que levei para armar o gravador .
Era um individuo adulto e provavelmente macho. 
O dia era de muito calor e com céu limpo e azul , e durante a gravação ainda estava escuro naquele trecho da mata .

1011409.rmk:
Begging call of a juvenile Tapera naevia (Striped Cuckoo) recorded in the open while being fed by Furnarius cinnamomeus (Pacific Hornero) in the buffer zone of the Área Protegida Privada Cazaderos, Zapotillo, Loja, Ecuador (200 m a.s.l.). This observation documents an active case of interspecific brood parasitism.

The chick was observed vocalizing persistently when the adult host approached with food. The vocalization is high-pitched, rhythmic and typical of food solicitation behavior.

Habitat: tropical dry forest edge, near agricultural matrix. Recording was made using the built-in microphone of a Samsung Galaxy Tab S7 FE. No playback was used.

This is possibly one of the first audio records of Tapera naevia’s begging calls in this context in southwestern Ecuador. No filtering or editing applied to the recording.

593319.rmk:
A very elusive bird; its plumage was not highly contrastant with the vegetation and it moved very rapidly from branch to branch. It sang very frequently from several perching points in the scrub vegetation, at ∼3-6 m in height. The scrub was on the border of a road in the countryside, and separate it from pastures. The area was formerly covered by bmh-MB. During my observations, it apparently was only resting and cleaning itself, alternating those activities with moderately long vocalization sessions. Some other species in the immediate surrounding environment were Tiaris olivaceus, Sporophila nigricollis, Zenaida auriculata, Columbina tapacolti and cf. Troglodytes aedon. I used a playback to provoque an answer call, but it didn't answer in response and limited only to look around to try to find the origin of the sound. 

Note: The recording was edited in Ocean Audio. I normalized it to -3 db and changed the recording format (mp3) into .WAV.

Courtship songs of three male doves closely following female doves. Perched low or walking on the ground near a large bamboo patch (1200 square meters) where several doves roosted. All White-tipped doves I saw in La Candelaria had bluish eye-rings.

703335.rmk: These are the vocalisations of a Boat-billed Flycatcher as it arrives at its roost site in a _Cecropia pachystachya_ tree. The first two vocalisations are fainter and made from another perch. The remainder of the vocalisations  are those made from the roost tree. The bird arrives at the roost after sunset, but when there is still some daylight, calls a few times, and then settles down silently to sleep. The recording was made at a known roost by leaving my iphone recording under the tree about 20 minutes before the bird was expected to arrive (no external microphone was used; volume was amplified to -3 db in Audacity). There is some distant background noise from a river.
